messages:
maria: hey all — just opened my first tiny refactor PR. quick questions: what's the preferred branch naming for small refactors, commit message style, and do i need to update any changelogs or ping specific teams? also how strict are we about squashing vs merge commits?
aj: welcome, maria! for small refactors we usually use refactor/<short-what> or chore/<short-what>. keep it short. example: refactor/remove-deprecated-cache-logic. commit msg: one-line present-tense summary, then blank line for details if needed. we prefer squashed merges for < 5 commits.

pre-commit hooks and local checks to run:
```
# run lint + tests locally
poetry run pre-commit run --all-files
poetry run pytest -q
```

if CI fails lint, run `pre-commit run --all-files` to autofix style.

CODEOWNERS controls required reviewers — check `/.github/CODEOWNERS` to see who to CC.

aj: also if you're touching runtime or model-serving bits, cc @olivia or @eng-runtime. otherwise pick one owner from CODEOWNERS. :thumbsup:
olivia: if it actually touches infra (deploy config, dockerfiles, model artifacts) ping me and i'll add the right reviewers. for pure code-style/refactor PRs you can tag me for a quick look but not required.
sam: changelog — we only add to changelog for user-visible changes or notable fixes. tiny refactors that don't change behavior: no changelog entry. if you altered a public API, add an entry under `CHANGELOG.md` in the unreleased section and mention in PR body.

maria: awesome, thanks. quick one — branch off main or staging?

aj: always branch off main unless you're doing a release/hotfix. staging branches are ephemeral and used by release engineers.
jun: CI note — if your PR changes dependencies run the integration job locally: `scripts/run-integ.sh` (it fires docker compose). otherwise tests in CI will cover it.

maria: got it. one more: PR title convention?

aj: title should be short and actionable: "Refactor: remove deprecated cache logic" or "Chore: rename xyz -> abc". include Jira/Ticket ID if applicable like `ENG-1234: Refactor...` in the title.
olivia: and in the PR description include: what changed, why, how to test, and rollout/rollback notes if relevant. a checklist helps: - run lint - run tests - update CODEOWNERS if new files - changelog if public API

maria: perfect. last practical: small PRs ok to self-merge after approvals?
aj: we don't self-merge unless you're an owner on that area. normally need 1 reviewer + green CI. owners or maintainers can merge after approvals. for doc/chore tiny fixes sometimes a single reviewer is fine.

dev-bot: CI: build passed ✅ (job #4821)

maria: thanks everyone! i'll update the PR description to include the checklist and ping olivia if anything runtime-adjacent shows up.

jun: welcome aboard, and ping me if you want a quick walkthrough of the repo layout — 10–15 min.
